subject: Request: Delivery-window exemption for async bulk inference (Helix Analytics)
messages:
From: Alice Gomez <alice.gomez@helixanalytics.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@helixanalytics.com
Date: Fri, 10 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Delivery-window flexibility for Helix bulk async jobs

Hi Vanessa / Rachel,

Quick context: Helix is moving a set of legacy nightly ETL pipelines to Redwood for model inference. Most runs are bulk/async (30k-200k records per job). Our procurement team needs to capture SLA language around job completion windows and retry guarantees; we have a hard requirement that 95% of nightly jobs complete by 06:00 PT, but we can accept longer tails for rare edge cases if there's a remediation plan.

Specific asks:
- Can Redwood commit an "async job completion window" for jobs sized like the attached sample manifest?
- What are recommended idempotency semantics for resubmits (we need deterministic at-least-once vs dedup behavior)?
- If completion misses the window, what credits/remedy would you propose (we need something we can present to our legal/finance team)?

We're aiming to finalize procurement language this week. Happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

Thanks,
Alice
Alice Gomez
Head of Data Platform, Helix Analytics

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Delivery-window flexibility for Helix bulk async jobs

Alice — thanks for the clear asks and the sample manifest. Looping in Marissa (CS lead) and Dev (platform) to capture the operational constraints and propose explicit contract language.

High-level: we can offer a bounded completion window with carveouts for overload/maintenance and an operational remediation plan rather than a strict per-job uptime SLA. To be concrete we should propose:
- A target: 95% of jobs (per daily run) finish within 4 hours of submission for manifests up to 250k rows (subject to a payload/sequence limit we can specify).
- Tail policy: jobs that miss 4 hours enter an accelerated retry/backfill path and are prioritized next-available capacity for completion; we can commit to an RTO (recovery time objective) of 12 hours for 99.9% of jobs when retries/backfill are invoked.
- Credits: pro-rated service credit if daily run misses the 95% bound for two consecutive days in a rolling 7-day window (we'll propose numbers once legal weighs in).

Please confirm whether the manifest patterns (batch sizes, per-row token estimate) in your sample are representative.

—Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Delivery-window flexibility for Helix bulk async jobs

Hi Alice — quick operational notes from CS and runbook implications.

Thanks for the manifest. Observations:
- Most jobs look I/O-bound with a heavy tail of long documents. For sizing we need an expected tokens-per-row and a max-seq length to set batching knobs.
- Idempotency: we'll recommend a client-supplied idempotency token on job submission + per-record stable ids in the payload. With that we can guarantee at-most-once application semantics in the user-facing output stream (server will dedupe by job-id + record-id).
- Retries: our platform supports automatic exponential-retry on transient infra errors (up to 5 retries) and a manual requeue path for business-logic failures. We'll add a visibility hook (webhook + job-status endpoint) so Helix can detect long-tail jobs and trigger compensating actions.

Proposed SLA text snippet (draft):
"Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to ensure that, for asynchronous bulk inference jobs submitted under this Agreement and formatted per the parties' manifest, at least 95% of jobs will complete within four (4) hours of job submission. In the event of a failure to meet this metric for two (2) consecutive days in any rolling seven (7) day period, Customer shall be entitled to a service credit as detailed in Schedule A. Redwood's obligation is subject to carveouts for force majeure, scheduled maintenance, and Customer payloads that exceed the tested manifest limits."

Attaching an internal runbook extract for retry behavior. Happy to update wording to match your procurement template.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is really helpful. A few follow-ups from procurement/ops:

1) Can you confirm the "per-manifest" limits you'd test against (max rows, avg tokens/row)? We need those numbers in the SOW.
2) For credits: procurement prefers a deterministic formula (e.g., X% credit of monthly bill per missed daily-run breach) rather than discretionary remediation. Can Redwood propose specific percentages for single-day and multi-day breaches?
3) During outages, will there be priority preemption so our nightly jobs jump to higher capacity once the platform is healthy again? If so, we'd like a timeline commitment for the preemption action (e.g., within 30 minutes of capacity availability).

Also copying our lead data engineer to discuss idempotency implementation details offline if needed.

—Samir
Samir Rao
Senior Procurement Manager, Helix Analytics

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Rao <samir.rao@helixanalytics.com>, Alice Gomez <alice.gomez@helixanalytics.com>

Subject: Re: Delivery-window flexibility for Helix bulk async jobs

Samir — appreciate the concrete asks. Below are the operational commitments Redwood proposes; please consider these proposed SOW bullets and we can convert to legal language next.

Operational commitments (proposed):
- Tested manifest limits: up to 300k rows per job; standard token estimate up to 1,500 tokens/row average (p95); if Customer payloads exceed either limit, the parties will agree on a separate sizing exercise.
- Completion window: 95% of jobs (per daily run) will complete within 4 hours of submission for manifests within the tested limits.
- Tail RTO: For the subset of jobs that miss the 4-hour window, Redwood will prioritize job requeue/backfill and will use accelerated retry lanes to aim to recover 99.9% of late jobs within 12 hours of submission.
- Preemption: When accelerated lanes are available, Redwood will preempt best-effort work and schedule backfill within 30 minutes of capacity announcement; preemption is subject to ongoing higher-tier SLA obligations and capacity constraints.
- Credits: Proposed deterministic credit: 5% of monthly bill for a single-day breach of the 95% rule affecting the Customer's daily run; 15% for two consecutive days; credits are capped at 30% per month.
- Idempotency / retries: Client must provide job-id + per-record id; server will dedupe on job-id + record-id and expose detailed job-status + per-record success/failure. Automatic infra retries: up to 5 attempts with exponential backoff.

Next steps: Rachel / Dev, can you confirm the feasibility of the 300k/1,500-token sizing and the 5/15/30% credit numbers from legal/finance? If we align, I'll ask Legal to prepare an amendment (attached draft).

Thanks — happy to jump on a resolution call today if that moves things faster.

—Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
